course_name_original: Ingeniería de Superficies, Recubrimientos y Adhesivos

learning_outcomes.text: Know and understand the fundamentals of surface science and engineering.
Know and understand the fundamentals of paint technology, its application, and legislation.
Know and understand the fundamentals of adhesion technology and its applications.

Adequately communicate knowledge, procedures, results, skills, and aspects of the surface engineering process in the field of Industrial Engineering, using appropriate vocabulary, specific terminology, and means.

Work effectively in multidisciplinary and multilingual environments, integrating capabilities and knowledge to make decisions related to the surface engineering process in the field of industrial engineering.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to surface properties and phenomena: Surface tension, capillarity, wetting, detergency, adsorption, adhesion, corrosion, ...
Surface engineering and modification of surface properties: Surface behavior. Surface characterization. Surface treatments. Coatings.
Paint technology: Composition and classification. Types of paints. Surface treatment according to substrates. Properties of liquid paint. Properties of dry paint. Application and legislation.
Adhesive technology: Adhesive joints. Design and evaluation of adhesive joints. Families of adhesives. Applications of adhesives.
New materials technologies: Composite materials and compatibilization techniques. Nanotechnology.
assessment_rules: For ordinary assessment, the final grade is composed of a written exam (60%) and continuous assessment (40%). A minimum attendance of 80% is required to pass the continuous assessment. If approved, the continuous assessment grade will be saved for the extraordinary convocation. Non-presentation to the written exam in the ordinary convocation will result in a "No Presentado/a" (NP) grade. For the extraordinary convocation, students who passed continuous assessment will have a final common exam (60%) plus their continuous assessment grade (40%); others will take a single final exam. Non-presentation to the written exam in the extraordinary convocation will also result in a "No Presentado/a" (NP) grade.
